A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same LEO-MINI work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LEO-MINI benchmark results, component and token-count ablations, efficiency measurements, qualitative examples, and expert-routing analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations and additionally reports GPU-memory measurements and comparisons of routing behavior with vanilla MoE.

M1.justification: COTR, the vision and LoRA experts, multimodal routing, the general expert, and three-stage training remain unchanged. The revised top-1 wording is consistent with k=1 already specified in v1; moving training into Appendix A.2 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same thirteen evaluation benchmarks and retain the LLaVA instruction data and EAGLE training-data settings. The added routing comparison uses the existing TextVQA, GQA, and ScienceQA tasks.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds LLaVA-HR to the general/MoVE benchmark comparison; v1 cited its paper but omitted this result row. V2 also introduces vanilla MoE into the routing-distribution comparison, beyond the retained LoRA-MoE performance ablation.

E3.justification: V2 adds GPU-memory usage as an efficiency metric in Section 4.6 and Table 4. The stated profiling setup remains the same: PyTorch Profiler, the image/question input, and one 48-GB A6000 GPU. Retained training and benchmark settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a comparison of MMOE-LLM and vanilla-MoE expert preferences, with paired routing plots and full vanilla routing distributions in Figures 8–9. Existing component, token-count, training-data, and qualitative analyses remain; v1's full routing plots are consolidated into v2 Figure 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Expert-choice distributions describe routing behavior rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged. V2 adds LLaVA-HR results, including MME 1554 versus LEO-MINI-Vicuna's 1543, changing that ranking. It adds memory results: 14.74 GB for LLaVA-Next, 20.10 GB for Eagle-X4-Plus, and 19.28/19.34 GB for one-/64-token LEO-MINI, plus vanilla-MoE routing findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9 are retained, including COTR attention and expert-output aggregation. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs, or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: conditional token reduction, multimodal expert routing with a general expert, and improved efficiency with strong visual reasoning. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2's appendix develops a comparative argument connecting additional input signals to more benchmark-dependent routing than vanilla MoE. The training-data discussion also drops the specific inference that more data improves visual summarization, retaining only improved performance. The original substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Training details move from Sections 3.4 and 4.1 to Appendix A.2 without changing their substance. Both specify the same training stages, data, LoRA rank, expert counts, balancing-loss coefficient, eight A6000 GPUs, and DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 setup.

R1.justification: V2 adds HAWAII and references on retrieval, hashing, and video grounding, mainly through a new broad contextual sentence in related work. It removes the Qwen technical-report and VQA references. The substantive positioning against token-compression and LoRA-MoE approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with targeted restructuring: training moves to the appendix, general-model comparisons receive Section 4.4, and efficiency follows qualitative analysis. Limitations become a separate section; generic potential-risk and acknowledgement sections are added, alongside author-date citation formatting.

P2.justification: The paper is substantially retypeset and its routing displays redesigned. Grouped plots become stacked bars, v1 Figures 7–8 are consolidated, and new comparison plots appear. Tables are resized and reformatted, the training table moves to the appendix, token-comparison delta rows disappear, and the efficiency table gains a memory column.

improvement.justification: The added memory measurements and vanilla-MoE routing comparison modestly improve empirical transparency and mechanism assessment. The gains are limited by unreconciled comparative prose: Section 4.4 still claims the best Vicuna MME result although the newly added LLaVA-HR row scores 1554 versus LEO-MINI's 1543. The core method and existing performance evidence remain unchanged.
